observations.observation: By Sep. 6, The Information had already reported roughly $517 billion in Anthropic compute deals. The May SpaceX report separately described up to $40 billion in payments and a 90-day cancellation right. Thus the later $518 billion headline alone was not wholly new public context; reported enforceability and payment terms were a more material information increment.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are media reports, not a retrieved contract ledger or public filing. Aggregates and terms may differ by agreement and reporting date.

observations.observation: TechCrunch’s Sep. 28 coverage says Reuters had first reported prospectus financial details on Monday and reports the $518 billion cloud, computing, and infrastructure plan. The underlying prospectus was described as confidential; the exact Reuters first-publication time was not established by the live pages reviewed.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The report concerns Anthropic’s aggregate future infrastructure plans and does not identify Micron as a supplier or quantify any Micron-related order, product, or shipment.

observations.observation: The same pre-cutoff TechCrunch article relays Financial Times reporting of $11.5 billion in Anthropic Q2 2026 revenue and a second consecutive quarter of operating profit on an adjusted basis, alongside Reuters-reported 2025 operating losses above $8 billion.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The profitability figure is adjusted and reported second-hand; it does not establish capacity utilization, cash coverage of long-term commitments, or any Micron-specific demand.

gaps: The confidential prospectus itself was not retrieved. The full filing passages, contract table, total calculation, and exact obligations remain independently unverified.

The Reuters syndicated result is dated Sep. 29 without a verifiable publication time, and the Sep. 29 Information SpaceX result lacks a visible date/time. The approximately 80% non-cancelable/pay-regardless detail and $84.5 billion SpaceX figure therefore cannot be placed with confidence before the cutoff from these pages.
No evidence found identifies Micron as an Anthropic supplier or connects the commitments to Micron HBM, DRAM, NAND, qualification, bit shipments, revenue, or capacity.
The retrieved material does not establish actual usage, delivery timing, capacity energization, cancellation or breach outcomes, or the amount of future cash paid in any particular period.
